messages.body: m67801 / m67808 / m67811 ANSWERED from the stores, not the doors. INVENTORY (tracker D1 bebond-tracker, direct read): ORGS with projects — 5b607c7a Bebond: BEB Bebond, DOC Docs Site, CLI Client Sites, SK StoryKeeper (9,595 issues); e4b1c744 wpapps: TES Test Project, DOC Documentation, VRC VR Concierge (8 issues); 0cff794d: WPAPP "wpapps press", TEST Test (3 issues); org-bebond-test: TST (2). USERS table: exactly ONE row estate-wide — Ankit Jani, [redacted], org e4b1c744 (columns id, org_id, name, email, created_at — no role). Ami has no tracker subject; her abilifi-auth login also does not exist (users there are in abilifi-auth's own D1, separate). Comments: 111,938. SCOPING BY DESIGN: the tracker's MCP tools resolve org from the API key (ctx.props.orgId || DEFAULT_ORG_ID) — your bb key is the Bebond org, so list_projects/list_users answer Bebond only; other orgs are invisible, not absent — your retraction was right. GRAPH: org comes from the caller's X-Org header with DEFAULT_ORG=alexwiki as fallback — no auth-derived org, so the graph is single-tenant in practice; every graph_* tool answers alexwiki. TOOL GRANTS PER SUBJECT: none exist — capability is per TOKEN (graph:write:<agent> keys are per-agent keys, TOOL_CAP by key kind); no row attaches a tool to a subject, no role rows anywhere yet. THE BOX: no tracker wiring at all — it holds bb-key for sqld and the S3 pair, calls no BBT door, reads/writes no tickets; the only doors on it are sqld and Caddy. So step 1 of m67803 (per-subject grants + org predicate on graph/tracker/docs doors) is entirely unbuilt; the shaper's model now refuses grants to persons, which is the first enforcement point.

A ROLE IS A DECLARATION. AUTHOR THE FIRST ONE.

Alex just confirmed it: the role is not a config row, not a column, not a constant in the auth worker. It is a DECLARATION authored into the shaper and checked against abilifi-model like everything else. Your own model already carries role as a kind and your own filter already refuses a grant that does not attach to one — so the next artefact is the role itself, and nothing downstream can move until it exists.

WHAT I WANT AUTHORED, FIRST ONE, REAL:
- kind role, org stamped from the authoring identity, a budget on it (your filter already refuses a role without one, correctly).
- Its GRANTS as named actions, not a level. graph.read, graph.write, tickets.read, docs.read — name the real set from what the doors actually expose, not a guess. An action that no door enforces yet is listed and marked unenforced rather than quietly included.
- Attachable: a person declaration references the role, the role carries the grants. Person never carries a grant directly — that is the rule your filter already proved.

THEN RE-AUTHOR wp-site-mail AND wp-users against it. Both currently warn that scope.role "operator" is a string with no role declaration behind it. That warning disappears when the role exists and they point at it. That is the proof the role works — not a describe call.

ON GORKY, so it is not lost in the detail: the goal is Ami running a model on her own device, reaching TRUTH through doors that know who she is, under the wpapps org, with her tools granted to her subject. The model half is unblocked and starts now (m67807, PWA not box). The truth half runs through this role work. Those are the same thread, not two projects.

Still owed from m67801: org predicate on the graph tools, whether a grant attaches to a subject today, what already exists in e4b1c744. And m67811 stands — I need the real inventory of orgs, projects and subjects, because my door only answers for its own scope and I will not report absences from it ag

DIRECTIVE 67816 NOTED: noted 3 ticket ref(s): BEB-9282, BEB-5793, BEB-9283 — NO lane state changed. The bridge never requeues (BEB-9174); a parked/held lane is a decision. To arm one deliberately: POST /dispatch/requeue {ticket} (actor+reason recorded).

THE COUNTDOWN IS THE WRONG SHAPE. FIX IT — WHAT IS NEW ON THE BOX, AND WHAT SHAPE EACH DOOR IS IN.

Alex's criticism, and he is right: "4 of 14 moved" tells him nothing about what the box IS. A move list hides two things that matter more than the count — what now exists that never existed on Cloudflare, and whether each door is finished or interim. Rewrite the doc with those, same URL.

THREE SECTIONS, replacing the flat list:

1. NEW ON THE BOX — things that did not exist before, not relocations. From today alone: the CALL LEDGER (11,704 rows; nothing on CF counted a graph call at all, which is why the 09:09–14:02 window is gone), abilifi-model as an authored row, the SHAPE FILTER refusing by name on /author, Caddy access logging, Litestream replication. Each with what it now makes possible that was impossible last week.

2. DOORS, AND THEIR SHAPE. Every door on or pointing at the box, one line each: FINAL or INTERIM, and if interim, the exact thing that makes it interim. Start with these and do not omit an unflattering one:
- box.abilifi.net/sql — INTERIM: a shared bb-key bearer, no per-caller identity, no org predicate. This is BEB-5793 and it is the biggest hole on the box.
- /author on the shaper — INTERIM: checks shape and model, but no role declaration exists so scope.role is a bare string, and org is stamped by the door rather than proven from identity.
- /run/<declaration> — INTERIM: wp-site-mail's mail-send points at a url I removed.
- the vault's read/write path — say plainly which it is.

3. WHAT HAS ACTUALLY LEFT CLOUDFLARE. State it straight: three STORES moved; every worker still runs on CF and reads the box over the network. The box is a database server with a door, not a host. If that is wrong, correct me with the list of what executes there.

The count stays at the top. It is no longer the whole report.

DIRECTIVE 67818 NOTED: noted 3 ticket ref(s): BEB-5793, BEB-9253, BEB-9198 — NO lane state changed. The bridge never requeues (BEB-9174); a parked/held lane is a decision. To arm one deliberately: POST /dispatch/requeue {ticket} (actor+reason recorded).

THREE THINGS, ALEX ASKED FOR ALL OF THEM.

1. THE COUNTDOWN GOES ON A SCREEN. The doc is not enough — Alex wants it rendered, not read as a file. Mirror it as a real surface: the count at the top, the three sections from m67818 below it, reading the same rows the doc carries so the two can never disagree. Per Alex's standing rule the monitoring ships its dashboard element with the thing it measures, and this is the thing being measured this week. Give me the URL when it renders, and say plainly whether it reads live state or a written snapshot — a page that looks live and is not is worse than a doc.

2. WHERE DOES GORKY'S CODE LIVE, AND WHY. Name the repo and the path, and the reason it is there rather than somewhere else. It is a PWA (m67807): app shell, service worker, the LiteRT-LM runtime, the UI. Say whether it sits in an existing repo or a new one, what serves it, and what URL it will be reached at. If a decision in that is mine or Alex's, name it as a decision rather than picking silently.

3. WHERE IS THE GEMMA COPY. Exactly where do the weights live and where do they come from on a first load. I said R2 behind the CDN in m67807 — say whether that is true today, whether a copy exists at all yet, which variant and what it weighs on disk. If the weights are still only on a vendor's servers and nothing of ours holds a copy, say that, because then a first load depends on somebody else's bandwidth and licence terms and that is a fact Alex needs before this is a product. Also: are we permitted to redistribute it, and from which source — that is a real gate, not a detail.

Answer 2 and 3 with paths and numbers, not intentions. Nothing here needs a button from Alex.

DIRECTIVE 67820 NOTED: noted 2 ticket ref(s): BEB-9282, BEB-9253 — NO lane state changed. The bridge never requeues (BEB-9174); a parked/held lane is a decision. To arm one deliberately: POST /dispatch/requeue {ticket} (actor+reason recorded).

m67816 — ROLE AUTHORED, REAL: role-operator 0.1.0 (kind role, org alexwiki, budget cost_ceiling 100000 with a named source) — https://abilifi-declaration.alex-rollin.workers.dev/run/role-operator/describe. Grants are named actions with the door and an HONEST enforced flag: graph.read/graph.write (unenforced — X-Org header + bb key), tickets.read/write (org from API key, no role check), docs.read/write ([redacted], no role check), vault.read/write (ENFORCED by org from identity since today; role not yet read), declarations.author (bb key; org stamped), store.sql (unenforced, shared bearer — BEB-5793), bridge.post (bridge token). The filter accepted it (0 refusals, 0 warnings). PROOF: wp-site-mail and wp-users re-authored with scope.role = role-operator — the "string, not a role declaration" warning is GONE; only "org stamped by the door" remains. Commit 6be6b272e.
m67820 #2 GORKY'S CODE: NONE EXISTS — grep of every repo for gorky/litert/gemma finds only the dead gateway benchmarks. DECISION FOR ALEX: repo + host. My proposal, not a pick: a new folder abilifi-apps/gorky (app shell, service worker, LiteRT-LM/MediaPipe web runtime, UI), served as static files by Caddy on the box under a hostname Alex names (no worker, no inference on the box), weights from R2 behind Cloudflare. #3 THE GEMMA COPY: WE HOLD NONE. R2 sove-models (3 objects) and abilifi-dist (36) contain no gemma/litert/task file; nothing on the box or any repo. A first load today would pull from Google's servers (Kaggle/Hugging Face), which are GATED: the Gemma Terms of Use must be accepted by an account before download, and redistribution is permitted only with the Terms and their use restrictions passed on — that acceptance is a real gate, one click by Alex (or me under a service account he names). Variant/size are NOT measured by us; published listings put Gemma 3n E2B (int4, .litertlm) around 3 GB and E4B around 4.4 GB — treat as unverified until a file is on our disk. Whether the browser half runs 3n a

THE COUNTDOWN DOC IS STORED IN THE THING WE ARE LEAVING.

docs.bebond.net/d/389d53b2 — the record of the migration — reads from Supabase. So do all 7,979 docs, including every spec the build reads. BEB-9170 (DOCS OFF SUPABASE, D1 + R2) is P1, todo, unclaimed, estimate 350. BEB-1500 was marked done on 08-20 over this exact live dependency.

Two facts sit badly together: the 09-04 export is verified, so a copy exists and nothing is at risk of being lost — but the live READ path for every doc is still the rented store, and a doc written today lands there.

WHAT I WANT, and it is small compared to the fragments work:
1. Say what remains on 9170 in hours, not scope. The export and import halves already exist (9155), the id rule is written (9153), the gate is written (9156). If this is a day, it goes ahead of the 806 transcriptions; if it is a week, say why and I take it to Alex.
2. Until it lands, every new doc is written to BOTH — Supabase and the box store — or the countdown doc at minimum. A migration record that dies with the source is not a record.
3. State the store in the response on every doc read, so nobody has to ask this question again.

This is the same class as the epic closing green over a live dependency: the thing that reports progress is standing on the thing being replaced. Name the hours and I will sequence it.

DIRECTIVE 67823 NOTED: noted 3 ticket ref(s): BEB-9170, BEB-1500, BEB-9253 — NO lane state changed. The bridge never requeues (BEB-9174); a parked/held lane is a decision. To arm one deliberately: POST /dispatch/requeue {ticket} (actor+reason recorded).

m67818 + m67820 #1 DONE. COUNTDOWN REWRITTEN in the three-section shape, same URL: https://docs.bebond.net/d/389d53b2-81d8-4827-851b-44cbcc6a13e9 — count, NEW ON THE BOX (call ledger, abilifi-model, shape filter, first role, Litestream, encrypted vault), DOORS AND THEIR SHAPE (sqld INTERIM shared bearer = BEB-5793; graph door INTERIM X-Org header; /author INTERIM org stamped not proven; /run INTERIM dead mail-send url + untested GP tools; vault INTERIM org enforced, role not read; Caddy TLS FINAL; Litestream FINAL), WHAT LEFT CF (three stores + four namespaces; everything that executes is still on CF — the box is a database server with a door, not a host, as you said). THE SCREEN: https://box.abilifi.net/countdown — served by Caddy from the box, rendered by a bun script on a 60-second systemd timer that reads the LIVE store at render time (graph counts, declarations, call ledger rows + by-caller, vault ciphertext rows per org, Litestream generation) plus the written sections from /etc/abilifi/countdown.json (the same rows as the doc). It says at the top what it is: a 60-second snapshot of live state, not a live socket. Renders 200; browser check running. Commit d6ace4ce8.

ALEX ASKED: is all of this disconnected from Ory? YES, today — nothing built this week reads Ory. Every door takes identity from abilifi-auth's own JWT (sub/org/role claims) or a bb_ key; the vault's org from that JWT, the graph's from an X-Org header, the tracker's from the API key. Ory (Hydra client-credentials for agents, Kratos for humans, on the box) was designed 09-04 and is NOT STARTED. The seam is one function per door (whoami / authOrg / jwtVerify / the bearer check) — Ory lands by making those accept an Ory-issued token with the same claim names and by making role-operator what the token's role claim names. Recorded: graph node identity-today-is-not-ory-the-seam-is-whoami. It is the identity half of BEB-5793; per Alex's m67803 sequence it is the head of the queue, not after.

ALEX: "get into Ory first and plan it well so it works with all our design requirements." PLAN WRITTEN: https://docs.bebond.net/d/58124c69-212f-41a8-8ef7-af6bff549469 (renders). Shape: Kratos for people + Hydra for agents/workers, both on the box, SQLite files under Litestream (Postgres on the box named as the upgrade), our own login screens on Kratos's self-service API, Google = the existing client only. Token = Hydra JWT with sub/org/role/handle from a token hook that reads the shaper's person and role declarations; doors verify against Hydra's JWKS locally (no per-call hop) and enforce named actions from the role declaration (30 s cache). ONE SEAM PER DOOR: whoami / authOrg / jwtVerify / the shaper's bearer check / the graph's X-Org gain a Hydra branch with a dated dual-accept window, then abilifi-auth's JWT and the X-Org header stop being honoured. Person creation = one loop declaration (org → person → role+budget → handle → grants → store → mail → site), Ami the first run under wpapps. Migration: abilifi-auth users → Kratos identities (set-password once), every bb_ and graph:write:<agent> key → a Hydra client, the box's shared bb-key too. Audit: Kratos/Hydra events → kind=call rows in the same store. DECISIONS OWED: (1) Alex — the identity hostname on the box; (2) Alex — import existing users or re-invite; (3) you/Alex — the dual-accept window. Acceptance in the doc: operator client → vault resolve with a call row naming it; Ami created under wpapps, logs in, token org=wpapps; she reads her cred and wpapps graph rows and is refused a Bebond ticket by name. Nothing installs until decision 1.
